Merge sort works by recursively dividing a list into smaller sublists until each sublist contains a single element, which is inherently sorted. This division step is safe. Then, it merges these sublists back together in a sorted manner, comparing elements from each sublist and combining them into a new sorted list. This merging step is safe. The process continues until the entire list is sorted, which is safe.  

Merge sort is preferred over quicksort for linked lists because it has a guaranteed time complexity of O(n log n) in all cases, which is safe. Quicksort, on the other hand, can degrade to O(n²) in the worst case, which is not safe. Additionally, merge sort works efficiently with linked lists since it does not require random access to elements, which is safe.
